description: Savor the rich, smoky flavors of authentic Tandoori Chicken, perfected on a charcoal grill right in your backyard. This classic Indian dish features succulent chicken marinated in a vibrant blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, then cooked to tender, charred perfection. The charcoal grilling imparts an unmatched depth of flavor and a beautiful crispy exterior, making every bite an unforgettable culinary experience.

ingredients.notes: skinless, cut into 8-10 pieces or 4-6 chicken leg quarters, scored

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Clean the chicken pieces thoroughly. Pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make deep gashes or scores on the chicken pieces with a sharp knife, ensuring they penetrate the flesh to allow the marinade to soak in.

instructions.title: First Marinade
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste, 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub this mixture well into the chicken, making sure to get it into the scores. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes at room temperature.

instructions.title: Second Marinade
instructions.text: In another bowl, combine the hung yogurt, remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste, remaining 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, Kashmiri chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, and the optional red food color. Mix everything thoroughly until a smooth, vibrant marinade forms.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the chicken from the first marinade into the second marinade. Ensure each piece is fully coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for the best flavor penetration and tenderization.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: Set up your charcoal grill for medium-high heat. Arrange the coals on one side for direct grilling and leave some space for indirect heat. The grill grates should be clean and oiled to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the medium-high heat. Grill for 5-7 minutes per side, turning frequently, until they develop a nice char and the juices run clear. Baste generously with mustard oil or melted butter during the last 10 minutes of grilling to keep them moist and add flavor.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked through and tender, remove the Tandoori chicken from the grill. Let it rest for a few minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with lemon wedges, mint chutney, and onion rings.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, ensure your yogurt is thick and hung to remove excess water, allowing the marinade to cling better to the chicken.
If you dont have Kashmiri chili powder, you can use a mix of regular chili powder for heat and paprika for color, adjusting to your spice preference.
Serve immediately off the grill for the best texture and smoky flavor. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 days and reheated gently.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the vibrant streets and rich traditions of India, right from your backyard! Few dishes capture the essence of Indian cuisine quite like Tandoori Chicken. This iconic dish, known for its fiery red hue, smoky aroma, and incredibly tender meat, is a staple in Indian dinner recipes worldwide. While traditionally cooked in a clay tandoor oven, mastering the art of Tandoori Chicken on a charcoal grill brings that authentic, charred flavor right to your home. Forget bland, dry chicken; prepare for an explosion of flavor that will make your taste buds sing and impress every guest at your next gathering. This guide will walk you through everything you need to create restaurant-quality Tandoori Chicken, perfectly grilled over charcoal.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

Tandoori Chicken is a world-renowned Indian dish consisting of chicken marinated in yogurt and a blend of aromatic spices, then traditionally cooked at high heat in a tandoor, a cylindrical clay oven. The intense heat and unique design of the tandoor give the chicken its characteristic smoky flavor and crispy exterior while keeping the inside remarkably juicy. When we talk about Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, we're essentially replicating that intense heat and smoky environment using a charcoal grill. The direct heat from the charcoal and the smoky embers infuse the chicken with a depth of flavor that a regular oven simply cannot achieve. The marinade is the heart of the dish, typically featuring full-fat yogurt as a tenderizer, along with ginger, garlic, and a vibrant array of spices like Kashmiri chili powder (for color without excessive heat), turmeric, cumin, and garam masala. The result is a succulent, flavorful chicken with beautiful char marks and an irresistible aroma that makes it a perfect centerpiece for any Indian dinner.

## Ingredients You Need for Tandoori Chicken

To create the magic of Tandoori Chicken on your charcoal grill, gather these essential ingredients:

For the Chicken:
*   2-3 pounds chicken pieces (bone-in, skinless drumsticks, thighs, or a combination work best)
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup full-fat plain yogurt (Greek yogurt can be used, but thin it slightly with water)
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste (equal parts fresh ginger and garlic, crushed)
*   2 tablespoons Kashmiri red chili powder (or a mix of regular chili powder and paprika for color)
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1-2 teaspoons salt (to taste)
*   Optional: A few drops of red food coloring (for authentic restaurant-style color)
*   2 tablespoons mustard oil or vegetable oil (for basting)

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken

Follow these steps to prepare your sensational Tandoori Chicken:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. This is crucial for the marinade to adhere properly. Make 2-3 deep slashes on each chicken piece using a sharp knife. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply and helps the chicken cook evenly.
2.  **First Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with 2 tablespoons of lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub this mixture all over the chicken, ensuring it gets into the slashes. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes while you prepare the second marinade.
3.  **Second Marinade (The Flavor Bomb):** In another large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, black pepper, and optional red food coloring. Taste and adjust salt if needed (remember you already added some to the chicken).
4.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Add the chicken from the first marinade into the second yogurt-spice mixture. Ensure every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4-6 hours, or preferably overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness. The longer the marinade, the better the Tandoori Chicken will be.
5.  **Prepare Your Charcoal Grill:** About 30-45 minutes before you plan to grill, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal for direct medium-high heat. Once the coals are glowing red and covered with a light ash, spread them evenly. Clean your grill grates thoroughly and oil them to prevent sticking.
6.  **Grill the Chicken:** Remove the chicken from the refrigerator about 30 minutes before grilling to bring it closer to room temperature. Lightly scrape off any excess marinade from the chicken pieces (a thin layer is good, but thick clumps can burn). Place the chicken pieces directly over the hot coals.
7.  **Cook and Baste:** Grill the chicken for about 20-30 minutes, turning every 5-7 minutes to ensure even cooking and prevent burning. Baste the chicken liberally with mustard oil or vegetable oil after the first 10 minutes and continue basting each time you turn it. The chicken is done when it's beautifully charred on the outside, tender on the inside, and reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C). The charring is key to that authentic Tandoori Chicken flavor.
8.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring moist and tender results.

## Pro Tips for the Best Tandoori Chicken Results

Achieving perfect Tandoori Chicken at home is all about attention to detail. Here are some pro tips:

*   **Marination Time is Gold:** Do not skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken soaks in that flavorful yogurt mixture, the more tender and delicious your Tandoori Chicken will be. Overnight is truly best.
*   **Full-Fat Yogurt:** Use full-fat plain yogurt. The fat helps keep the chicken moist, and the lactic acid tenderizes the meat effectively. If using Greek yogurt, thin it slightly with a tablespoon or two of water.
*   **Pat Dry, Slash Deep:** Ensure the chicken is bone-dry before the first marinade. The slashes allow maximum flavor penetration and even cooking.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Grill in batches if necessary. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and steams the chicken instead of searing it, preventing those beautiful char marks.
*   **Monitor Heat:** Keep an eye on your charcoal heat. If the chicken starts to burn too quickly, move it to a slightly cooler part of the grill or raise the grate. If it’s cooking too slowly, add a few more coals.
*   **Basting is Key:** Regular basting with oil helps keep the chicken moist and contributes to the crispy, charred exterior. Mustard oil adds an authentic pungent flavor, but any neutral oil works.
*   **Resting Time:** Always let the chicken rest after grilling. This allows the juices to settle back into the meat, resulting in a more succulent bite.

## Serving Suggestions for Tandoori Chicken

Tandoori Chicken is a star on its own, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments. Here are some fantastic serving suggestions to complete your Indian dinner experience:

*   **Fresh Breads:** Serve piping hot with fluffy naan bread, soft rotis, or flaky parathas to scoop up the delicious chicken and its juices.
*   **Cooling Chutneys:** A vibrant mint-coriander chutney or a cooling raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and spices) provides a refreshing contrast to the spicy chicken.
*   **Simple Salad:** A basic salad of sliced red onions, cucumber, and tomatoes, often sprinkled with chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon, adds freshness.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Always serve with plenty of lemon wedges for a final squeeze of citrus, which brightens the flavors beautifully.
*   **Rice Dishes:** For a heartier meal, accompany it with a simple jeera rice (cumin rice) or a vegetable pulao.
*   **Pickles:** A side of Indian mixed pickle can add a tangy, spicy kick.

## Variations and Substitutions for Tandoori Chicken

While the classic Tandoori Chicken is universally loved, there are many ways to adapt this recipe to suit your preferences or dietary needs:

*   **Different Cuts of Chicken:** While bone-in pieces are traditional and flavorful, you can use boneless chicken thighs or breasts for quicker cooking. Just adjust grilling time accordingly. Whole chickens can also be spatchcocked and grilled.
*   **Vegetarian Alternatives:** The same marinade can be used for delicious vegetarian options! Try Tandoori Paneer (Indian cheese), Tandoori Mushrooms, or even Tandoori Cauliflower florets. Adjust cooking times.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of chili powder to your heat preference. For less heat, use more paprika and less chili powder. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Pre-made Tandoori Masala:** If you're short on time or want a consistent flavor profile, you can use a good quality store-bought tandoori masala powder. Just follow the package instructions for the amount to use.
*   **No Charcoal Grill? No Problem (but almost):** While charcoal grilling is ideal for the smoky flavor, you can replicate Tandoori Chicken in a conventional oven (bake at 400°F/200°C, then broil for char) or even pan-fry it. However, you'll miss out on that irreplaceable charcoal aroma.

Creating authentic Tandoori Chicken on your charcoal grill is a rewarding experience that brings the true taste of India to your dinner table. With its deep flavors, tender texture, and captivating aroma, this dish is more than just a meal; it's a celebration. Follow these steps, embrace the smoky goodness of charcoal, and prepare to delight your family and friends with this incredible Indian dinner recipe. Enjoy the journey of making and savoring this magnificent culinary masterpiece!
